name: Western Ghats (Nilgiri / Silent Valley region)
blurb: Rainforest fruit, shola grassland, macaques, tahr and tigers.

tip.title: Lose the Cullenia flowers
tip.text: Silent Valley's lion-tailed macaques depend on Cullenia flowering. Set Cullenia to -100% and watch the macaque, then the leopard and viper that eat it.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Western Ghats, Silent Valley National Park, Lion-tailed macaque). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.name: Wild figs
nodes.desc: Fig trees fruit heavily and feed many forest primates, bats and birds. GloBI records macaques and langurs eating banyan figs.

nodes.name: Jamun
nodes.desc: A fruit tree eaten by elephants, macaques and langurs in GloBI records.
A megaherbivore that grazes and browses on many plants and eats fruit. The Western Ghats hold the largest wild population in India.

nodes.name: Gaur
nodes.desc: A huge wild ox of Western Ghats forests and hill grassland, living on grasses, herbs and shoots.
A large forest deer that browses and grazes. It is a key prey of tigers and dholes in GloBI records.
A big lizard that eats insects, frogs, eggs and small animals, and also scavenges carrion.
A pack-hunting wild dog that preys on sambar, muntjac and wild boar in GloBI records.
The top predator of the Ghats forests, taking sambar and gaur, and sometimes elephant calves where ranges overlap.
A flexible hunter that GloBI records eating monkeys, giant squirrels and sambar.
Moist Arabian Sea air is forced up the Ghats and drops heavy rain on the western slopes.
Periodic fire helps keep montane grassland open, though too much burning shrinks shola forest.
Nutrient-rich soil under rainforest and shola, kept in place by roots and moist leaf litter.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter and dead animals and return nutrients to the soil.

story: The Western Ghats, or Sahyadri, run 1,600 km along India's west coast and cover 160,000 km² across six states. They formed when India separated from the supercontinent Gondwana. Anamudi, at 2,695 m, is the highest peak.
matters: Silent Valley National Park in Kerala protects part of the range, in the Nilgiri hills. The lion-tailed macaque is endemic to the Western Ghats.
